title: Cap. III Sol. close: why not pardoned alike — beneplacitum; Augustine profundum; defer De Reprobatione
pass_a_gloss: Further, I will also add this: If it be asked, Why did this wretched one undergo the sentence of death? it is rightly answered, Because he was a robber and a traitor. But if it be asked, Why did the King not will to pardon him alike as the other who was in the same case? why not to affect him with the same honors? Here we cannot answer except ineptly, Because he was guilty of robbery and of injured majesty; for so also was that other whom we have formed in thought. But it must be answered, Because it seemed good to the King for his good pleasure to have mercy on the one, not to have mercy on the other. But the reason of this discrimination lies hidden in the casket of the Royal breast, it is not founded in the diverse merits of the persons. I seal this answer with that saying of Augustine, Why he frees this one rather than that, or does not free, let him scrutinize, who can, so great a depth of his judgments, yet let him beware the precipice; Epistle 190. But when we shall have come to our other thesis, On Reprobation, we will explain these things more clearly.
pass_b_english: Add this: ask why the wretched man suffered death — rightly, Because he was robber and traitor. Ask why the king would not pardon him as he did the other in the same case, or heap the same honors on him — here to answer Because he was guilty of robbery and treason is inept (so was the other we imagined). The answer is: it seemed good to the king, of his good pleasure, to pity the one and not the other. The reason of that discrimination lies in the king's breast, not in diverse merits. I seal it with Augustine (Epist. 190): why he frees this one rather than that, or does not free — let whoever can sound that great depth of his judgments, yet beware the precipice. When we reach our other thesis, On Reprobation, we will unpack this more clearly.
source_text: Porro, et illud adjiciam: Si quaeratur, Cur miser iste sententiam mortis subiit? recte respondetur, Quia latro et proditor erat. At si quaeratur, Cur noluit Rex perinde illi ignoscere atque alteri qui in eadem causa fuit? cur non iisdem honoribus afficere? Hic non possumus nisi inepte respondere, Quia latrocinii et laesae majestatis reus erat; sic enim et ille alter quem cogitatione informavimus. Sed respondendum est, Quia visum est Regi pro suo beneplacito alterius misereri, alterius non misereri. Hujus autem discriminis ratio latet in scrinio Regii pectoris, non fundatur in personarum diversis meritis. Obsigno hanc responsionem illo Augustini dicto, Cur istum potius quam illum liberet, an non liberet, scrutetur, qui potest, judiciorum ejus tam magnum profundum, veruntamen caveat praecipitium; Epist. 190. Sed cum ad alteram thesin nostram, De Reprobatione, ventum fuerit, haec explicabimus magis enucleate.
